We have decided to use CAMEO to make our software designs and export the work we do into an SDD document. Cameo has many different templates which dictate how the exported document looks. However, none of them provide all the things we desire in an SDD. In order to fix that, we are making our own custom template.

A Cameo template can be opened up as a word doc and it is populated with templating language called velocity template Language(VTL). Look online for resources to understand and modify this language.

Critical faults not specified in the derived requirements.

EST SS requirements that specify a fault condition such as EST_212 need a corresponding derived requirement to generate that critical fault condition. This is important because ESATP_1597 specifies that commanded movement to the FAD motor servo valve will be disabled when ESTAP detects a critical fault, but no derived requirements actually generate a critical fault, only alarms. These newly derived critical fault requirements should be children of the applicable parents and the alarm requirements should only be children of EST_116.

column1: Resolve chain of dependencies in controller common
column10:
D454 SSW project space of DEV OQE as we R&D.

Our project wiki is on Confluence: https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/display/DS/D454+SSW+Team+Home

Our process continuous improvement project "ACE" (Atlassian Center of Excellence) may be found here: https://192.168.3.34/jira1/secure/RapidBoard.jspa?rapidView=3&projectKey=ACE
column37:
Currently, the controller common repo is very delicate to version bumps to select crates. This is problematic because:

(1) there can only exist 1 version of a crate within the same workspace (this includes versions of crate dependencies pulled from remote registries).

(2) Upon updating/version bumping a crate, all 1st party crates in the workspace that use that crate as a dependency need to be version bumped as well. This produces a cascading effect where a chain of crates with diverging paths need to be version-bumped even when making code changes to single crate.

 

Proposed solution: break-up the chain. Move commonly used ( and rarely changing) API types and functions to a separate crate such that when logic change are made to nio_api_wrapper (where these exports might otherwise be exposed), for example, this does not need to cascade down to our wide collection of dependents and sub-dependents of these API types.
column121:
New crate created for defining and exposing common defined types imported across various crates across the common repo. The new crate is written idiomatically following our Rust coding and doc guidelines.

Common repo pipeline still passes

Merged into mrg/signal_stim_interface_and_mock_nio_changes

column37:
The IRQ service does not work for bonded interfaces. The Service must be able to determine if there is a bond and if there is, it must be able to get the slave interfaces associated with the bond. Once the slaves are identified, the IRQs associated with the slaves can be set to a specific core. 

 

ChronyD affect PTP and causes time jumps which mess with the NIO and controller syncronization.

 

Firewalld prevents UDP packets from being sent.

example for script:
{code:java}
#!/usr/bin/bash
# This script performs per-boot tuning of RT# Set RCUs
for i in `pgrep rcu[^c]` ; do taskset -pc 0 $i | true ; done
echo "Successfully set RCUs"# Tune IRQs
ens=$(ip -o addr | grep 10.22 | head -1 | awk '{print $2}')

slaves=($(ip addr | grep "$ens state" | awk -F ":" '{print $2}'))

export CORES="${RT_ISOLATED_CORES:-}"

if [[ -z $CORES ]]; then
    echo "Error: RT_ISOLATED_CORES not set"
    exit 1
fiecho "Applying RT tuning for cores $CORES"for slave in "${slaves[@]}"; do
        echo "hello"
IRQS=($(sudo tuna show_irqs | grep $slave | awk -F " " '{print $1}'))    # 
for each irq set irq to core
    for IRQ in "${IRQS[@]}"; do
        echo "hello"
        echo "sudo tuna move --irqs=${IRQ} --cpus=${CORES}"
        sudo tuna move --irqs=${IRQ} --cpus=${CORES}
    done
done
exit 0 {code}

column37:
The signal map logic was designed to have signal groups where you could map different input/output signals to each other so that we could set and assert multiple values across multiple signals. Each signal group is given a vector of values to set and assert against, an index to loop through each vector, and the size of the vector of values. Once the index reaches the end of the vector, the test harness deems that this signal group has passed the test since it has set and asserted all values for each output and input card respectively.

 

The one issue with this design is when you want to only have an output signal that maps to no input signal. With no input signal, the test harness cannot assert the value at an index and therefore can never advance to the next index. This causes the test harness to run forever since the index will never reach the end of the vector.

 

There are two solutions for this bug:
 # Fix the signal map logic
 ## You can make it so signal groups that only have output signals associated with it to pass once the value has been set
 ## Make the discrete cards capable of performing init register logic (DPAZMINO'S FAVE)

The way parasoft works is by running a server that our pipeline jobs can communicate to in order to ensure our code base is MISRA Compliant. Upon performing the checks, a MISRA finding report will be generated that tells you how compliant the codebase is. 

 

There is a RPM for setting up parasoft: [https://192.168.3.19/ssw-phc-developers/server-configuration/roles/parasoft]

 

May or may not work, but is a good point to begin at. Upon it not working, there are some parasoft conflunce pages that can be used to gather more information.
[https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/spaces/DS/pages/110989294/Official+Parasoft+Notes]

This epic is a continuation of the SSWSW-10668 milestone. This epic only include updating the RTMB Adapter with TBD/unimplemented proto files.

 

*Summary:*

With the PHC3/MES PaaS merger, an opportunity has arisen to simplify communication between controllers/services across the system. The Interlock Service is being rebranded as the Real Time Message Broker to better capture its purpose, and will serve as the message broker for system states required by hosted segments. This milestone captures the work associated with the development of the real time message broker. We expect to use RabbitMQ as our message broker, but may need to write supplemental software for alerting. There is an Architecture Working Group associated with this effort that includes representatives from OII, LM, and GDMS. Much of the details of this milestone will be filled in by working group activities.

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve:
 * Simplifies the many-many event-driven communication paths between hosted segments using a heavily used system design pattern.

How does this fit into the larger project:
 * Hosted segments need data from each other in order to make decisions about what operations can or cannot be performed. The amount of data paths makes it difficult to create several point-to-point systems, and since all segments are now residents of the MES PaaS, a single, central data exchange service can be stood up.

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview:
 * Update SRS
 * Create Design
 * Create acceptance test plans
 * Implement Design in Feature Branch(es)
 * Write acceptance tests
 * Integrate with LM

Key Components/Docs/Specs:
 * PHC3 SRS
 * NDS ICD

*Risks and Considerations*
 * Execution of this milestone is heavily dependent on working group output/pace.

*Completion Criteria*

CI/CD

 * SRS Updated

Specs

Outputs

column37:
The issue: currently, the ESTAP's command interface integration of the Controller Simulink model results in a tray motion profile where the tray will incrementally be ordered to move 0.5 inches while a Manual Mode order stream is open; however, due to some behavioral constraints of the Simulink Controller model's API this will result in a jerky tray motion profile. Essentially, the tray will move 0.5 inches -> slow down as it approaches the target -> stop -> then repeat similar start-move-stop cycles of movement for as long as the order stream is open. 

 

Fix estap v0.13.1 to handle Manual Mode streamed commands in a way that produces a consistent tray motion profile in which the EST reaches and maintains the max nominal velocity for L/L and FAD movement for the duration that an uninterrupted Manual Mode order stream is open.

Changes should be tactical quality as eventually we intend to have the latest version of estap absorb these changes.

column37:
The BIT (Built-In Test) of the CMDO42 works by writing a value and reading that value back. If the value read back does not match the one written after a certain amount of time, then there is an issue with the card.
 
At the moment, the NIO only produces an error to tell the controller that the card is erroring in general if the data that was previously written does not equal the value read back. However, It can be determined which of the 64 channels on the CMDO42 is producing an error by checking with specific bit does not match. The NIO needs to be updated in order to generate this more granular diagnostic routine to produce errors based on the individual channel instead of at the card level.

The catenary display is a separate widget that displays the Sub and ROV locations in respect to the ocean surface and floor. The ROV position is shown near ship, far ship, and measurements from the ship. This display widget is located in the SAD GUI project repo on Penpot.

The dark grey line curving from the ship to the ROV is the umbilical. It will always be slightly curved due to the ocean current. The orange, blue, and pink lines are for measuring the ROV distance relative to the ship. There are two additional measurements; sail to surface and ROV to seafloor. The two dashed lines are the sea surface and sea floor.

column37: There is a requirement in the NIO ICD for reporting error 044 when multiple cards contain the same VME addresses on an NIO. This error is suppose to be checked per NIO and is not suppose to fail if there are cards with the same VME address who belong to different NIO's. Upon running the latest version of the UMS config file, It was discovered that the current implementation performs this check regardless of the NIO a card belongs to. The two NIOs in the UMS config file have cards that are exact duplicates for redundancy. Therefore, they share the same VME Address to access the same card which causes the 044 error. Before merging the UMS Configuration File into development, this problem must be fixed
column121:
'- Fix VME address duplicate error 044 which causes the error to happen across multiple NIO's instead of just one

- merge into dev

It has been discovered that the LBTF/HIL Lab analog cards can be slightly out of calibration. It was tested via the G4 - V420 wire that an output of 100 Ohms from the V420 caused a input from the G4 of 97.16 Ohms which is within a tolerance range of 2.84%. 

All analog cards are expected to have some sort of out of calibration range. Each signal group will have the tolerance key. If no key is found, default tolerance will be 0. Checks will be added to the hIl_test function to check that analog has a non zero tolerance while discrete/serial signals only every have a tolerance of 0, otherwise exit fatally.

The TCAP is comprised of the TCAP controller and TCAP Graphical User Interface (GUI). The TCAP GUI is what the operator uses to control the movement of the tube 9 and tube 10 hatches. It is responsible for providing the visuals needed to for operators to conduct SSW mission operations. The TCAP GUI allows operators to view the live status of the Tube Control System (TCS).

The purpose of this milestone is to document the design, implement and test the Overrides unit of the TCAP GUI.

Summary:

The ESTAP is comprised of the ESTAP controller and ESTAP Graphical User Interface (GUI). The ESTAP GUI is what the operator uses to control the movement of the tube 9 and tube 10 hatches{color}. It is responsible for providing the visuals needed to for operators to conduct SSW mission operations. The ESTAP GUI allows operators to view the live status of the External Stowage Tray System (ESTS). It also allows operators to move the tray and override sensor values. The purpose of this milestone is to document the design, implement and test all the units of ESTAP GUI.

Each page that is displayed will be considered a unit. We will need sub-unit pages to capture specific/key variations of a given unit page. Should be re-evaluated before tasks are added into the PI.

column37: All the HIL tests have been created but cannot be ran on the LBTF due to the way we designed the tests originally. We use card Id's to set and get data and HIL tests are designed to test all signals. However, LBTF will only test tactical signals and most signals will not be connected to its STIM counter parts due to this reason. Therefore we must make the HIL tests generic to the point where we set and get data at the signal level in order to ensure that tests work on both sets of hardware without any issue. All HIL tests must be updated in order to use this new design. Config maps must also be updated in order to allow us to implement and use this new design. Signal ID's will be used to create mappings. For example, a tactical signal will be given an ID of lets say 0x0000 and its STIM signal counterpart will be given a signal ID of 0x1000. A tactical signal with ID 0x0123 will mapped to STIM signal ID 0x1123 and so on and so forth. On initialization of the test harness, we will loop through all output signals (using nio.get_cards().get_card_signals() and filtering via signalType) from NIO 1 (tactical signals) and NIO 2 (STIM signals) in order to create a map of Output signals that will map to input signals. This will allow the testing of data at the signal level and this map will be used to perform all sets and gets within out tests.

column37: All the HIL tests have been created but cannot be ran on the LBTF due to the way we designed the tests originally. We use card Id's to set and get data and HIL tests are designed to test all signals. However, LBTF will only test tactical signals and most signals will not be connected to its STIM counter parts due to this reason. Therefore we must make the HIL tests generic to the point where we set and get data at the signal level in order to ensure that tests work on both sets of hardware without any issue. All HIL tests must be updated in order to use this new design. Config maps must also be updated in order to allow us to implement and use this new design. Signal ID's will be used to create mappings. For example, a tactical signal will be given an ID of lets say 0x0000 and its STIM signal counterpart will be given a signal ID of 0x1000. A tactical signal with ID 0x0123 will mapped to STIM signal ID 0x1123 and so on and so forth. On initialization of the test harness, we will loop through all output signals (using nio.get_cards().get_card_signals() and filtering via signalType) from NIO 1 (tactical signals) and NIO 2 (STIM signals) in order to create a map of Output signals that will map to input signals. This will allow the testing of data at the signal level and this map will be used to perform all sets and gets within out tests.
column121:
'- rename SBC_tests folder to be hsit_tests if not done so already
- rename hsit folder under old SBC_tests folder to be hil if not done so already
- Update config map to align with new signal id mappings. All tactical signal ID's will be given an ID value within the range of 0x000-0x0FFF and will be mapped to STIM ID's within the range of 0x1000-0x1FFF. (see more details in description) In order to ensure all config maps do not overlap signal ID values, the range for E7 signals will be assigned a range for 0x700-0x7FF.
- Create a directory in src/core_loops and include/core_loops called HIL if does not exist already
- Add a cpp and hpp file for the card under test in the appropriate HIL subdirectory under src/core_loop and include/core_loop 
- Create a generic run loop file for HIL tests and generic run loop function in the run loop file if it does not already exist. This function will be the entry point for all individual HIL tests for each card for LBTF. They can be individually selected to run via the -t flag. Only 1 card will be tested at the a time. It is uncertain whether the master test plan will be its own test or the running of all card tests at once.
- Create test based on the test plan: https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/display/DS/SRS+Testing#SRSTesting-NIO-UMS-LBTF-Timing-Test
- Move existing card specific functions (such as hsit_e7_test() in hsit_e7_run_loop.cpp/hpp) into the new files you created under the appropriate HIL subdirectory

*Point Estimate:  ~12 pts*

*Priority: High*

*Summary:*

The External Stowage Tray Program (ESTAP) is dependent on the Simulink EST Controller Model for correctly outputting motor voltages that move the EST. The Systems team irregularly delivers Simulink EST Controller Model releases to us that we need to test and integrate into the ESTAP. New releases of the Simulink EST Plant Model might also be delivered complimentary to the controller model. In the event of a model delivery, changes to the model's API must be examined, wrapper crates must be updated, and updated wrapped crates must be integrated into ESTAP. Intermediary testing to confirm that a new model itself as well as its wrapping is done correctly. Acceptance tests that simulate tray movement (dependent on the EST Controller Model) must be updated and pass. This work deals with *Unsafe Rust; hence, it is strongly advised that any development work done for updating the wrappers and integrating the model into the ESTAP is performed by the most experienced Rust developers.*

Additionally and regardless of whether a new release is actually delivered, design pages need to be produced for the EST Controller Model wrapper crates as well as for the ESTAP's simulink module. 

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve
 * Enables mechanical EST movement such that any produced motion profile satisfies ESTCS requirements.

How does this fit into the larger project
 * This work is critical to the mechanical movement of the EST. Behavioral correctness of the ESTAP cannot be assumed for the FST unless the latest release of the Simulink EST Controller Model is integrated.

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview
 * Write the design pages for the ESTAP's simullink module and Simulink EST Controller Model wrapper crates 
 * If a new release is delivered, critically examine changes to the model's API, update the wrapper crates, and integrate into the ESTAP
 ** Update acceptance tests to account for any potential breaking changes (especially relevant in the case where is a new plant model release as well) 

Key Components/Docs
 * ESTAP SRS
 * [simulink_module|https://192.168.3.19/ssw-phc-developers/controllers/estap/-/blob/mrg/port-estap-sswctl/tactical/estap/src/simulink.rs?ref_type=heads]
 * [controller_smest_api|https://192.168.3.19/ssw-phc-developers/controllers/simulink/-/tree/development/tactical/controller_smest_api?ref_type=heads]
 * [libcontroller-smest-sys|https://192.168.3.19/ssw-phc-developers/controllers/simulink/-/tree/development/tactical/libcontroller-smest-sys?ref_type=heads]

*Risks/Considerations/Dependencies*
 * Simulink generated code does not behave correctly and or has performance issues
 ** Debugging issues related to the generated code can be very time consuming
 * Inexperienced Rust developers are performing the necessary development work
 ** Simulink models and processes for integrating them not widely understood by overall team

*Completion Criteria:*
 * Upon receiving a new model release:
 ** Wrapper crates and integration into the ESTAP are updated
 ** Acceptance tests are updated and pass in the pipeline
 * Design pages are created and adjudicated ({*}Needs to be done regardless as whether a new release is received{*})

Outputs
 * Acceptance tests for ESTAP that confirm that EST movement ordered via manual and automatic mode controls correctly move the tray to target positions and do so with a tray motion profile (velocity, responsiveness, etc) that satisfies ESTCS requirements. 
 * Associated software design documentation produced.

*Point Estimate:*  

*Priority: High*

*Summary:*

The ESTAP Controller currently receives order from the ESTAP GUI without validating that the order is allowed to be performed. The ESTAP needs to receive a order message from the ESTAP GUI and validate if that order can be performed or not. If the order can be performed the ESTAP will respond with no error code, but if it cannot be performed the ESTAP should return an error code indicating such to the ESTAP GUI and the ESTAP will trigger a fault and send an alert message to the alert service. Currently the ESTAP does not have a mechanism to determine which ESTAP GUI is the primary GUI and is able to control the EST. This will need to be implemented to ensure that only one GUI can command the system at a time (this will be in a sperate milestone) and this logic will need to be added into the order validity used by ESTAP. This milestone covers implementing the order validity from the ESTAP SRS for each command that can be received from the ESTAP GUI. 

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve
 * Adds the order validation needed by the tactical ESTAP controller to ensure commands are only performed when it is safe to do so.
 * Burns down unimplemented ESTAP SRS requirements. 

How does this fit into the larger project
 *  The ESTAP needs to validate orders received via its gRPC command interface to ensure that it is allowed to perform the action requested.

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview
 * Implement and test the ESTAP command validity requirements in the ESTAP SRS. 

Key Components/Docs
 * ESTAP SRS
 * interlocks.rs
 * ESTAP commands module (to be replaced by "orders" module)

*Risks/Considerations/Dependencies*
 * The order validity in the ESTAP SRS has not be fully reviewed by collaborators for correctness.

*Completion Criteria:*

CI/CD
 * Acceptance tests are added to the ESTAP integration branch pipeline

Documentation
 * Test Plans are created for each acceptance test for the approved format

Specs
 * Rust code is written idiomatically
 * Code is free of errors and follows the Rust coding guidelines
 * All code is covered by unit tests
 * All unit tests include AAA comments following the approved format

Outputs
 * The ESTAP controller correctly validates each command for validity
 * Acceptance tests are implemented and passing for each SRS

*Point Estimate:*  

*Priority: High*

*Summary:*

The TCAP Controller currently receives order from the TCAP GUI without validating that the order is allowed to be performed. The TCAP needs to receive a order message from the TCAP GUI and validate if that order can be performed or not. If the order can be performed the TCAP will respond with no error code, but if it cannot be performed the TCAP should return an error code indicating such to the TCAP GUI and the TCAP will trigger a fault and send an alert message to the alert service. Currently the TCAP does not have a mechanism to determine which TCAPP GUI is the primary GUI and is able to control the TCS. This will need to be implemented to ensure that only one GUI can command the system at a time (this will be in a sperate milestone) and this logic will need to be added into the order validity used by TCAP. This milestone covers implementing the order validity from the TCAP SRS for each command that can be received from the TCAP GUI. 

*Project Impact:*

 * Adds the order validation needed by the tactical TCAP controller to ensure commands are only performed when it is safe to do so.

 *  The TCAP needs to validate orders received via its gRPC command interface to ensure that it is allowed to perform the action requested.

column37: All the HIL tests have been created but cannot be ran on the LBTF due to the way we designed the tests originally. We use card Id's to set and get data and HIL tests are designed to test all signals. However, LBTF will only test tactical signals and most signals will not be connected to its STIM counter parts due to this reason. Therefore we must make the HIL tests generic to the point where we set and get data at the signal level in order to ensure that tests work on both sets of hardware without any issue. All HIL tests must be updated in order to use this new design. Config maps must also be updated in order to allow us to implement and use this new design. Signal ID's will be used to create mappings. For example, a tactical signal will be given an ID of lets say 0x0000 and its STIM signal counterpart will be given a signal ID of 0x1000. A tactical signal with ID 0x0123 will mapped to STIM signal ID 0x1123 and so on and so forth. On initialization of the test harness, we will loop through all output signals (using nio.get_cards().get_card_signals() and filtering via signalType) from NIO 1 (tactical signals) and NIO 2 (STIM signals) in order to create a map of Output signals that will map to input signals. This will allow the testing of data at the signal level and this map will be used to perform all sets and gets within out tests.

column37:
Follow-on task to SSWSW-10856 and SSWSW-11688.

We need a client wrapper library for the Signal Stim Interface that will abstract away details concerning exact signal lineups and controller logic for triggering particular faults in the TCAP or ESTAP. The user of this client wrapper's library will simply use its API to invoke faults selected from various enumerations representing different fault categories. The intention behind the library is to support easy usage of the interface by non-system owners who do not need to know the specific low level details; however, methods and types for using the raw interface will still be exposed. This provides the user freedom of choosing to target specific signals should library's high-level abstraction be too constraining.

The client wrapper will be written in Go and published to the package registry upon a merge into the repo's development branch.

In particular, this task will produce the overall structure of the library, will include an initial limited selection of faults, and will expose the raw types and RPCs of the Signal Stim Interface. 

The client wrapper library will provide an API for:
 * Creating an interface client
 * Injecting:
 ** ESTAP fault conditions
 ** TCAP fault conditions
 * Removing:
 ** specific previously injected fault condition 
 ** removing all faults conditions 
 * Using the raw interface functionality

Initial faults categories included by object ID:
 * ESTAP
 ** ESTAP_991
 ** ESTAP_992
 ** ESTAP_993
 ** -ESTAP_994-
 * TCAP
 ** TCAP_1454
 ** TCAP_4255
 ** TCAP_1456
 ** TCAP_1457

- initial included TCAP fault categories: TCAP_1454, TCAP_4255, TCAP_1456, TCAP_1457
- raw interface types and RPCs are exposed to provide flexibility to the user

column37:
*Summary:*

Following the 25% Gate HMI review teams received direct feedback from the customer and from sailors to increase customization options. SSW has decided to create a prototype to align with a more flexible and modern product

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve:
 * Best foot forward approach. Meet the customers standards. Secure work

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview:
 * There will be two review periods. Material will be created at the 2 week mark for internal review and comments and then again at the PI 17 review for the government. Customer/sailor feedback has been used to drive user stories and workflows

{*}Action 1{*}: Camera Views to be dynamically allocated based on what they provide.

There are two approaches we should take for this.
 * Tube and Tray Control screens should be updated to contain an icon that when clicked would display live video feed of a subset of cameras. For example, clicking this icon near the Tube 10 bottom hatch will display the live video feed for relevant cameras.
 * We should put together Tube or Tray screen with a modified layout which by default displays live video feed. The exact view should be selectable by the operator.

{*}Action 2{*}: Concept behind better usage of the touch screens at the ROV workstations.

The touch screen should be used as a nominal operations touch screen. The touch screens should primarily contain controls. All needed statuses should be provided by the primary display in front of the operator. I would imagine the need to create modified UI Designs containing just the controls for Tube 10 Bottom hatch operations and Tray Auto Sub Mode operations.

{*}Action 3{*}: Moveable widgets, to give operators control over what their display would look like.

The intent behind this is clear. The operator would like some control over the layout of the screens in front of them. The best approach to present this concept would be for SW to put together a rough demonstration of this functionality to the operator.

column37:
*CARD NOT FOUND PART:*

We need to prepare all HSIT Tests to be ran on the LBTF Rack. The Card not found tests do not require a new configmap_values.yaml since it relies on having a card with an incorrect VME Address. Therefore, each configmap_values.yaml needs to only be checked to ensure that the VME Addresses are still incorrect if ran on the LBTF rack. 

 

*NON CRITICAL FAULTS PART:*

The non critical fault test needs a new configmap_values.yaml. The new one, like the original one, will contain a G4 and a CMDO42 card. The VME Addresses must be updated to align with what is found in the LBTF Rack. The ethernet_ports section must be fitted to have one correct port and an incorrect port.

This test asserts that upon detecting an non critical error such as ethernet link failure or card faults, the NIO will report these issues, but continue operating as normal.

The G4 card fault that is being tested is the open detection fault which is caused by not having the channel physically connected to a sensor. Therefore, the LBTF G4 card used must have a channel that is not connected to anything. If this channel is not the first channel, then the test must be updated to assert the channel in use. (see image below)

!image-2026-02-16-11-37-08-324.png!

The G4's in SBC-A (where the test runs in the pipeline) do not have anything connected so changing the channel used in the test will not break anything. Only updates to the configmap_values.yaml must be made so the test ran on the LBTF and SBC-A use and test against the same channel.

- Create a new configmap_values.yaml for the non critical faults test to run on LBTF rack. This test requires a G4 and CMDO42 Card with correct VME Addresses.
- Update all tests accordingly based on needs (see description for details)

*Summary:*

There needs to be an update to the NIO/NIO API in order to more generically initialize/configure specific channels on cards. It has come to our attention that cards can have each channel connected to a unique sensor/electrical segment which can require unique configuration. This functionality for configuring a channel independently is crucial for allowing the NIO to successfully interface with each sensor/electrical segment.

What Problem Does this Solve:
 * The NIO/NIO API needs to be updated to handle configuring different channels on a card which will prepare us for the second iteration of LBTF

column37:
A feature providing the server-side implementation of the Signal Stim interface in the Mock NIO. The implementation will exist in its own module that exposes an API for modifying status message signal data based on injected signal values extracted from client requests.

The module's API should abide by best practices for API design. Preexisting logical paths in the Mock NIO should not be altered – no breaking changes to the app itself. Inclusion of API function calls from the new module will be conditionally invoked based on usage of a CLI flag, and when enabled, will only be invoked at initialization (starting up the server request listener) and immediately before sending out a status message. Internal logic of the interface's server implementation will be executed in a separate tokio task that will not interfere with core logic of the Mock NIO.

column243: 05/Aug/26 9:45 PM;bpember;Changed design from combining topic names with the same rate in a thread to each topic name getting there own thread. This is because there is a big difference between a tokio thread and a os thread. An os thread takes about 2MB of memory. A tokio thread is not a real os thread, its a task (rust future) and is about a few kilobytes of memory. Tokio uses a work stealing scheduler which looks at all active tasks and distributes them acorss all available cpu cores. By combining multiple publishers in the same thread you will have head of line blocking as each publish is async blocking which might cause late messages to go off the publish rate. So its better to separate them to prevent any blocking and timing issues and since the tokio threads are lightweight cpu performance is not an issue.;;;

*Point Estimate:  9 pts*

*Priority: High*

*Summary:*

The ESTAP and TCAP need to report health and status of their respective systems to the MES Health and Status Service. This includes both the physical and software components health and status.  The Health and Status Interface developed in this Epic will provide a generic interface for communicating with the service that will be integrated into both ESTAP and TCAP. We expect that implementation details will not vary too much between the controllers in how they interface with the service, and otherwise traits will be leveraged to fill in any gaps.

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve
 *  Health and Status for ESTAP and TCAP will be implemented in accordance with the MES requirements.

How does this fit into the larger project
 * This partially completes the current Health and Status requirements for both ESTAP and TCAP.

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview
 * The health and status interface sends the health and status information of the ESTCS and TCS to the MES Health and Status Service.

Key Components/Docs
 * MES Health and Status SDD (Current: X:\Eng.440\Projects-VA\VA SSW\CWS Working Group\Meetings\Arch_WG_2024\SPLINTER\Health&Status\Meetings\2026-01-12)
 * MES IRS (TBD Link)

*Risks/Considerations/Dependencies*
 * Updates to the Health and Status Protos
 * Health and Status is delivered in the MES PaaS
 * Unknown date for the MES IRS

column37:
Investigate is there is more sauce we can add to make NIO cracked on linux 

"In traditional, memory management implementations using demand paging, allocating memory upfront was still
not enough since the operating system would initially map that memory in the swap file; also, only the portions of the
application that were run during initialization may be present in physical RAM with the remainder mapped to the
applications image on disk. An RTOS using demand paging would also need to provide a mechanism that forced the
RTOS to place all of the application's virtual memory into physical RAM. Furthermore, a real-time application would
need a guarantee from the operating system that it would not later swap portions of the application's virtual memory
back to the filesystem. This mechanism is most commonly called a memory lock. Linux does provide memory locking
using the mlockall() system call. A real-time application should call mlockall(), shortly after the start of the process
or thread, with the options MCL_CURRENT | MCL_FUTURE. Those options assure that all current and future pages
allocated to the process or thread are locked into physical RAM. This call is recommended even when the system is
configured with no swap because Linux can still swap executable pages to their file images in the file system. "

 

"Setting up a pod with a real-time scheduling policy in Kubernetes requires configuring the underlying node to support real-time tasks (usually via a {{PREEMPT_RT}} kernel) and ensuring the container has the necessary privileges to request real-time scheduling policies like {{SCHED_FIFO}} or {{SCHED_RR" - this may be key to remove offset from the recv nio status message. }}

*Summary:*

Code coverage for the NIO/NIO API repository is now reported in the pipeline and every merge requests shows that there is around 50% coverage. Moving forward, unit test will be added so that this number goes up until it becomes 100%. Once our coverage reaches 100%, all new code that is untested will cause the pipeline to fail in order to ensure total coverage, code quality . 

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve:
 * The NIO/NIO API code base is not fully unit tested

How does this fit into the larger project:
 * Updates to our unit test to provide 100% coverage will allow for more confident deliveries of the NIO due to extensive testing.

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview:
 * Create Unit tests for files currently not tested
 * Update existing unit test for files to improve converage

column37:
*Summary:*

With the PHC3/MES PaaS merger, PHC3 is now losing the full OS and cluster, becoming a "real time region" (RTR) within the MES PaaS. As a result, the following capabilities need to be developed in the context of the MES PaaS:
 * Kubernetes Core Allocation
 * RT OS Configuration
 * BIOS Configuration

There is a working group associated with this effort involving LM, EB, and GDMS.

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve:
 * Provides real-time capability to the MES PaaS.

How does this fit into the larger project:
 * The MES PaaS is now hosting the real time control systems, and therefore needs to have dedicated real-time nodes configured to support the controllers' timing requirements.

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview:
 * Update SRS
 * Generate BIOS Configuration
 * Create Kubernetes Core Allocator Design (Native vs. Plugin TBD)
 * Create RT OS Design
 * Create acceptance test plans
 * Implement Design in Feature Branches
 * Write acceptance tests
 * Integrate with LM

Key Components/Docs/Specs:
 * PHC3 SRS

*Risks and Considerations*
 * Execution of this milestone is heavily dependent on working group output/pace.

*Completion Criteria*

CI/CD
 * Acceptance tests passing in pipeline

Documentation
 * Design pages produced
 * SRS Updated

Specs

*Summary:*

The MSOS Operating room contains several cabinets each containing an environmental monitoring device. This device measures things like temperature and detects things like circuit breaker flips. A service must be developed to interface with the environmental monitors and distribute the data to GUIs and the MES Health and Status service.

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve:
 * Gives operators visibility into cabinet conditions

How does this fit into the larger project:
 * In the MES merger discussions, EB fought to develop the environmental monitoring software for our hardware. LM decided that we should just do it for all the hardware, since it should be the same for everything. As a result, we are now developing the environmental monitoring service for the entire MES PaaS.

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview:
 * Update Requirements
 * Create Design
 * Write test plans
 * Write software
 * Acceptance Test
 * Integrate

column37:
*Summary:*

With the PHC3/MES PaaS merger, an opportunity has arisen to simplify communication between controllers/services across the system. The Interlock Service is being rebranded as the Real Time Message Broker to better capture its purpose, and will serve as the message broker for system states required by hosted segments. This milestone captures the work associated with the development of the real time message broker. We expect to use RabbitMQ as our message broker, but may need to write supplemental software for alerting. There is an Architecture Working Group associated with this effort that includes representatives from OII, LM, and GDMS. Much of the details of this milestone will be filled in by working group activities.

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve:
 * Simplifies the many-many event-driven communication paths between hosted segments using a heavily used system design pattern.

How does this fit into the larger project:
 * Hosted segments need data from each other in order to make decisions about what operations can or cannot be performed. The amount of data paths makes it difficult to create several point-to-point systems, and since all segments are now residents of the MES PaaS, a single, central data exchange service can be stood up.

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview:
 * Update SRS
 * Create Design
 * Create acceptance test plans
 * Implement Design in Feature Branch(es)
 * Write acceptance tests
 * Integrate with LM

Key Components/Docs/Specs:
 * PHC3 SRS
 * NDS ICD

*Risks and Considerations*
 * Execution of this milestone is heavily dependent on working group output/pace.

*Completion Criteria*

CI/CD
 * Acceptance tests passing in pipeline

Documentation
 * Design page produced
 * SRS Updated

Specs
 * TBD

Outputs
 * Design Document
 * Requirement Updates
 * RTMB Deliverable

column37:
This initiative is focused on getting out HSIT Acceptance tests, one for each card, running on the LBTF/Sim Rigs.

This initiative delivers end-to-end hardware/software integration testing using representative hardware (UMS NIO is LBTF) connected to simulation hardware through tactical-style wiring harnesses. The goal is to validate real signal interfaces, timing, and simple control behavior across the full chain – from software commands and simulated plant responses to physical I/O, harness integrity, and observed hardware reactions – under realistic operating conditions. Testing will focus on proving functional correctness, interface compliance, and robustness (including fault handling) while generating traceable evidence that the integrated system behaves as intended before higher-level qualification and field deployment to GDMS.

h4. Description
*Point Estimate:  13 pts*

*Priority: High*

*Summary:*

Currently the [ESTAP|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/display/DS/ESTAP] and [TCAP|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/display/DS/TCAP] report and receive data needed for system interlocks through the PHC3 Interlock Service. This service is changing to the Real Time Message Broker (RTMB). The RTMB will be the service that sends out ESTAP and TCAP output data to other hosted segments and Ships Control System (SCS) as well as sending interlock related data to ESTAP and TCAP.  This milestone covers updating the interlock_service_interface crate to be compatible with the new interface.  

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve
 * Helps fulfill RTMB interface requirements for ESTAP and TCAP.

How does this fit into the larger project
 * This partially completes the MES IRS RTMB requirements for both ESTAP and TCAP by providing a common API that enforces the required interface.

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview
 * The RTMB Interface and Design Page document and provide the ability to send and receive data to other hosted segments on MES and SCS through the RTMB.

Key Components/Docs
 * [https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/display/DS/RTMB+Design+Notes]
 * [https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/display/DS/Proposed+SRS+Requirements] 
 * MES IRS (link TBD)

*Risks/Considerations/Dependencies*
 * Lack of developer knowledge of the tokio, tonic, traits, and prost
 * Changes to the architecture of the RTMB 
 ** It being removed for another solution. 

*Completion Criteria:*  

Specs
 * Created using the approved [Design Page Guidelines|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/display/DS/Design+Doc+Guidelines]
 * Rust code is written in accordance with the [Rust Coding Guidelines|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/display/DS/%28WIP%29+Controller+and+Rust+Documentation+Guidelines]

Outputs
 * Design page created to document the design of the common RTMB interface
 * The interlock service crate has been updated to send and receive data from the RTMB

column37:
Due to the way staging branches are structured, and the want to only rerun unit-functional jobs on change, the "compare_to" field of the change rule needs to be dynamic on pipeline creation. This is accomplished by a "meta" gitlab job that fills in a gitlab ci yml template and triggers a child pipeline using the filled in template. This has been prototyped in controller common. This architecture also opens up other opportunities for more parts of the pipeline to be dynamic. For example, matrix jobs can be populated based on the actual files in the repo as opposed to being hardcoded, avoiding the problem of needing to update the matrix when new things are added.

This task involves identifying areas of the pipeline that should be dynamic and creating the meta jobs.

 

Resource:

[https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/pipelines/downstream_pipelines/#dynamic-child-pipelines]

[https://192.168.3.19/ssw-phc-developers/controllers/common/-/pipelines/46158]

column37:
Due to the way staging branches are structured, and the want to only rerun unit-functional jobs on change, the "compare_to" field of the change rule needs to be dynamic on pipeline creation. This is accomplished by a "meta" gitlab job that fills in a gitlab ci yml template and triggers a child pipeline using the filled in template. This has been prototyped in controller common. This architecture also opens up other opportunities for more parts of the pipeline to be dynamic. For example, matrix jobs can be populated based on the actual files in the repo as opposed to being hardcoded, avoiding the problem of needing to update the matrix when new things are added.

This task involves identifying areas of the pipeline that should be dynamic and creating the meta jobs.

 

Resource:

[https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/pipelines/downstream_pipelines/#dynamic-child-pipelines]

[https://192.168.3.19/ssw-phc-developers/controllers/common/-/pipelines/46158]

column37:
*Summary:*

Our current CI/CD process is not staged (i.e.: all lints/tests are ran on every development merge). Moving forward, we would like to speed up the iteration process for developers by separating out levels of testing and mapping them to different branches. This means that acceptance tests will run on merges to integration, and errors will be kicked back in the form of new tasks. Developers will only need to verify to the unit/functional level (can manually run acceptance tests if updating/implementing them). Staging will also allow us to implement a pre-release versioning scheme that maps to the larger project CI/CD process.

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve:
 * Slow merge process into development

How does this fit into the larger project:
 * Updates our versioning scheme and mapped level of confidence to be aligned with the larger project

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview:
 * Create prototype CI/CD design
 * Implement each stage in a feature branch
 * Merge the feature branch, go through the process, and fix bugs

column37:
Design an application that will verify if applications stay pinned to cores (this is the gist but the spike will inform more specific information).

Include information reference to the type of kubernetes resources needed and potential libraries to use. Include details on Concept of Execution.

Specifics are TBD on spike linked to task

 

If putting info in a repo, put it in testing

UNOFFICIAL design page (aka no meeting but can use design page template)

 

Assumptions of application:
 # Kubernetes cluster with scheduler exists
 # some form of core allocations exists

Functionality:
 # when deploying a new RT app, need to ensure it's deployed on a unique, isolated core
 # need to think about what to do once run out of cores
 ## Need to determine expected behavior of RKE running out of cores to use
 ### Most likely pod will be in a pending state (unable to be currently scheduled)

 

[https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/display/DS/Real+Time+Region+%28RTR%29+Test+Harness]

^ Need to design test controller and test apps

Test controller is its own deployment (runs forever) or job (runs until not needed anymore)
 * can think of it as a test harness for the kubernetes scheduler

Steps of what will happen in the test
 # Test controller deployed
 # 1 test app deployed
 # test app reports back to controller about node/core affinity
 ## node affinity = knowing which node (server) it's running on
 ## core affinity = knowing which core it's running on
 ### can potentially grep a file to find out
 # test controller scales (aka deploys another test app)
 # Verify new test app is on a different core
 # repeat steps 3 to 5

 

*First priority:*

Test application NEEDS to determine that RT app is on a UNIQUE core (doesn't need to be a knower of all cores, but should check current RT app against other deployed apps to make sure it's not trying to use an already used core)

*Second priority:*

Test application potentially be a knower of isolated cores.

Isolated cores that RKE would attempt to run apps on: core 6 - 13

Controller needs to assert that the RT app has not been deployed on non-isolated cores

There should be a file to read which cores are isolated

 

Context:

We will either use a custom plugin OR native Kubernetes capability for core allocation. This test will NOT be responsible for assigning cores and should be agnostic to the core allocation process. Should read back returned info from RT app about which core it's on and assert that it's a unique, isolated core.

Test controller reads file to receive list of isolated cores

Test controller deploys RT App

RT App reports node and core affinity to test controller

Test controller compares RT app core to array of occupied cores (currently empty)
 * if core not in array
 ** if core isolated
 *** add core to array
 ** if core not isolated
 *** test fails
 * if core in array, test fails
 * if app returns and is in pending state (no cores available for pod to be scheduled), that means RKE has run out of cores
 ** test passes?
 ** should the test controller know how many cores exist and deploy a fixed number of RT apps? or should it simply iterate through cores until no more are available and pass at the end?
 *** most likely latter

 

Diagram flow of test controller:

Test controller → Kubernetes scheduler → deploys RT app pod

RT app pod → node/core affinity to test controller → Kubernetes scheduler → deploys next RT app pod

 

Diagram flow of rt app:

column37:
Right now, the NIO child pipeline has 3 jobs that perform unit test coverage, and one job "combined coverage" that combines them and generates a final coverage number for the entire NIO repo. This final number needs to appear in the MR overview page:  !image-2025-11-18-13-40-21-933.png!

 

Right now, it doesn't appear there, despite the coverage print and regex matching:

!image-2025-11-18-13-40-53-661.png!!image-2025-11-18-13-41-03-601.png!

 

The theory is: the "Coverage: number%" being in the child pipeline is causing an issue such that gitlab cannot see it and cannot parse it. Need to figure out how to make this accessible to the parent pipeline. Idea: caching

 

Cache the coverage number, then have the parent pipeline access the cached number and make sure gitlab can read and parse it.

*Summary:*

Perform a Hardware Software Integration Test (HSIT) in accordance with the HSIT Card Test Plan for the Commercial Off The Shelf (COTS) VME Cards. This test will validate the all NIO card drivers. 

*Project Impact:*
What Problem Does this Solve:
 * Performing this test will provide Objective Qualifying Evidence (OQE) that NIO card drivers satisfy the requirements of the SRS.

How does this fit into the larger project:
 * Performing the test and obtaining OQE for NIO drivers will allow for continued testing of the NIO with more complex applications.

*Implementation Overview:*
High Level Overview:
 * OQE for the NIO and drivers will be collected and placed in a common location for data collection, and analysis.  All data, analysis, and findings will be summarized in a formal test report.

Key Components/Docs/Specs:
 * OQE test data.
 * Operation Manual for all COTS Cards: 
 ** North Atlantic Manual: [64C3-Operations-Manual-2017-05-08-1111.pdf|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/download/attachments/110986017/64C3-Operations-Manual-2017-05-08-1111.pdf?version=1&modificationDate=1742989828349&api=v2]
 ** CM-DO-42 Manual: [CM-DO-42-USERS-MANUAL.pdf|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/download/attachments/110986017/CM-DO-42-USERS-MANUAL.pdf?version=1&modificationDate=1742989828259&api=v2]
 ** IP330A Manual: [IP330A_804e_User_Manual.pdf|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/download/attachments/110986017/IP330A_804e_User_Manual.pdf?version=1&modificationDate=1742989828337&api=v2]
 ** IP440A Manual: [IP440A_User Manual.pdf|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/download/attachments/110986017/IP440A_User%20Manual.pdf?version=1&modificationDate=1742989828333&api=v2]
 ** IP445A Manual: [IP445A_User_Manual.pdf|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/download/attachments/110986017/IP445A_1029.pdf?version=1&modificationDate=1742989828318&api=v2]
 ** IPwd8630A Manual: [User Manual_IP-WD-8530 & 8630-G-x-1.7.pdf|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/download/attachments/110986017/User%20Manual_IP-WD-8530%20%26%208630-G-x-1.7.pdf?version=1&modificationDate=1742989828281&api=v2]
 * Operation Manuals for Stimulation Cards:
 ** TBD as part of the Test Plan
 * [NIO CSCI|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/display/DS/NIO+CSCI]

*Risks and Considerations*
 * Execution of the test plan is heavily dependent on having all stim cards and wiring/cables fully functional (debugged) and ready for testing. In addition, stim card drivers that initialize and run stims are required prior to testing. 

*Completion Criteria*

CI/CD
 * TBD

Documentation
 * OQE that all drivers and VME card functionality meets the SRS.

Specs
 * Test Plan must adhere to the Card Manual specifications. Cards to be tested must be correctly paired with cards designed to stimulate each respective card.

Outputs
 * OQE for each card and it's subsequent driver will be collected and documented as determined by [(High Priority) PI13 HSIT Card Test Plan - 33 Points|https://192.168.3.34/cnfl1/display/DS/%28High+Priority%29+PI13+HSIT+Card+Test+Plan+-+33+Points].

column37:
Due to the way staging branches are structured, and the want to only rerun unit-functional jobs on change, the "compare_to" field of the change rule needs to be dynamic on pipeline creation. This is accomplished by a "meta" gitlab job that fills in a gitlab ci yml template and triggers a child pipeline using the filled in template. This has been prototyped in controller common. This architecture also opens up other opportunities for more parts of the pipeline to be dynamic. For example, matrix jobs can be populated based on the actual files in the repo as opposed to being hardcoded, avoiding the problem of needing to update the matrix when new things are added.

This task involves identifying areas of the pipeline that should be dynamic and creating the meta jobs.

 

Resource:

[https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/pipelines/downstream_pipelines/#dynamic-child-pipelines]

[https://192.168.3.19/ssw-phc-developers/controllers/common/-/pipelines/46158]

29/Oct/25 11:07 AM;dpazmino;An assumption has been made when the test plan was created that writing a logical '1' to a CMDO42 channel will produce a logical '1' in the associated CMDI40 channel. This may be incorrect.

!image-2025-10-29-11-07-52-313.png!

This screenshot above is from the CMDI40 manual and according to this 3rd paragraph, a logic '0' read back means that the channel is being driven by an input voltage. A logic '1' means the channel has no voltage driving it.

 

In the CM DO 42 manual (image below), each channel controls a relay which is a fancy word for a switch. By writing a logical '1' you can power the channel which turns the relay on.

!image-2025-10-29-11-08-11-676.png!

Normally when a relay or switch is on, power can flow as shown below.
